title: Relating Cover & Interior Formats
slide_intent: Teach designers to plan a cover and its interior together so readers can see a relationship as they turn the page.
strategic_value: NASA can use a publication’s own structure to give the cover a recognizable connection to the contents.
demonstration: Three labeled rows pair a cover with a facing interior spread. Red lines connect a square-image alignment, a top-hanging arrangement and a horizontal center-line arrangement.
practical_value: Choose the interior’s strongest alignment, then carry it onto the cover. Compare both side by side before finalizing either layout.

content_islands.name: Relationship guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the heading at upper left and describe the three alignment alternatives across the top.

content_islands.name: Square-image alignment
content_islands.spec: Pair the cover with its spread in row a. Extend the guides across the gap so the cover image shares visible alignments with interior elements.

content_islands.name: Top alignment
content_islands.spec: Use row b to hang heads and text from the top and hold photographs at the bottom.

content_islands.name: Center-line alignment
content_islands.spec: Use row c to extend a horizontal center line across cover and spread, with images and text breaking above and below it.
